comment: The grammars the Prism reads its content by, each the specifications' own ABNF taken from their pinned text by tools/standards/grammar.py (tools/standards/abnf.py) and written to out as data for site/read/abnf.mjs. texts: each specification, pinned by SHA-256, and the sections whose rules it contributes (all, when none are named). lends: a text whose rules are taken only where the others refer to them (RFC 5234's core rules). bindings: a rule its specification states in prose, given here in ABNF with the reason, so a machine can match it; each must replace a prose rule. headers: the header fields the grammar defines, each by the literal its rule opens with ("Date:"), the current rule first and its obsolete form (RFC 5322 section 4) after. zones: RFC 5322 section 4.3's obsolete zone names, from its own sentences. witnesses: where to write, for each rule, the shortest field or message the grammar derives through it, so a suite can show the reader matches every rule.

grammars.title: Internet Message Format header fields (RFC 5322, RFC 6532's UTF-8, RFC 2919's List-Id, RFC 5234's core rules)

utf8-2: RFC 3629 section 4's two-octet sequences, as the code points they encode: the page reads decoded text, where a UTF-8 sequence is one character
utf8-3: RFC 3629 section 4's three-octet sequences, as the code points they encode (surrogates are not characters)
utf8-4: RFC 3629 section 4's four-octet sequences, as the code points they encode
